findings.location: README 'W02e K1: boot entries' row ('nor hand init an environment', 'W03 widens the grammar only through a reviewed schema revision'); model comment line 62; vectors A08 and V67
findings.finding:
(a) console= adds a unit. systemd v256 getty-generator instantiates serial-getty@<tty>.service for every non-VC console in /sys/class/tty/console/active. So A08 (console=ttyS0,115200) adds serial-getty@ttyS0.service on the enrolled boot. That unit is a login service, and W01 §5.2 S2 orders containment before every login service.
(b) 'nor hand init an environment' depends on kernel configuration. unknown_bootoption (v6.12 init/main.c) hands selinux=1, enforcing=1 or lockdown=integrity to init's envp when CONFIG_SECURITY_SELINUX_BOOTPARAM, CONFIG_SECURITY_SELINUX_DEVELOP or CONFIG_SECURITY_LOCKDOWN_LSM is not built. The names are inert for systemd. Without LOCKDOWN_LSM the lockdown word also has no effect, so the observed hardening.lockdown remains the evidence. No allowlisted bare word reaches init's argv: ro, rw and quiet are consumed by __setup or early_param.
(c) The grammar lives only in the model (KERNEL_PARAMETERS). The v3 schema is unchanged, and its kernelCmdline pattern ^[ !#-&(-~]+$ admits every refused word. So 'a reviewed schema revision' cannot widen the grammar, and a consumer that validates only against the schema does not enforce it.
(d) V67 (the maintenance unit twice) is refused 'maintenance boot entry does not select the maintenance target', although systemd would select it. The refusal is conservative; only the message is wrong.

findings.finding:
The list of installed and firmware state that still decides the unit is incomplete.
- SystemdOptions, without Secure Boot: proc_cmdline_parse reads the variable first for every caller (PID 1, debug-generator, import-creds, fstab-generator, getty-generator). So systemd.wants=, systemd.mask=, systemd.set_credential(_binary)= and rootflags= in it apply, not only systemd.unit=.
- System credentials. v256 src/core/import-creds.c imports:
  - SMBIOS type-11 OEM strings and qemu fw_cfg credentials on any host that is not a container or a confidential VM, regardless of Secure Boot;
  - /.extra/credentials, placed by sd-boot or sd-stub.
  debug-generator turns systemd.extra-unit.* and systemd.unit-dropin.* credentials into units and drop-ins. This reaches round-4 E6's effect without a command-line word.
- R4-1 asked for 'installed init= alternatives'. The statement names the initrd's own handling, but not the root's /sbin/init.
systemd.import_credentials=no would close the credential channel from the command line, but that word is outside the grammar.

questionAnswers.Q0:
The README dispositions are true in the round-5 bytes.
- The model enforces exactly the listed allowlist.
- '--' and every later word, systemd.*, rd.* and SYSTEMD_* words, runlevel words and every other KEY=value are refused.
- MAINTENANCE adds systemd.unit=planeon-maintenance.target exactly once, and ENROLLED must carry lockdown=integrity.
- V61 to V68 are added and A08 is rewritten. RUNLEVEL_TARGETS is removed and the V17 wording is fixed.
E1 to E6 and M-a to M-c are refused, and so are 30 further ENROLLED tokens and 8 MAINTENANCE tokens from earlier rounds. R4-1 and R4-2 are CLOSED, and no earlier CLOSED item reopened.
The grammar does still leave quote-free words that add or select units (R5-1):
- rootflags= values: x-systemd.requires=, wanted-by=, required-by=, after=, before= and makefs become dependencies of, or on, sysroot.mount in a systemd initrd;
- tree selection: X-mount.subdir= and btrfs subvol= in rootflags=, and root= and initrd=, which nothing ties between the two entries.
console= instantiates serial-getty@<tty>.service through getty-generator. This is benign, but it is a login unit (R5-2).
Init and the security state:
- no allowlisted word reaches init's argv;
- allowlisted keys reach init's environment only on kernels that lack their handlers, and are then inert;
- no allowlisted word weakens lockdown (lockdown_param only raises) or SELinux (selinux=1, enforcing=1 and security=selinux only enable; context mount options need ':').
Legitimate entries: none is refused that W03 could not avoid. The nearest are:
- '+' in Debian 13 kernel-install initrd paths;
- rd.luks.*, rd.lvm.* and kernel hardening parameters, which W03 can replace with initrd configuration and kernel config, or admit through the widening path;
- GRUB's BOOT_IMAGE=; the loader is already scoped to systemd-boot (R5-4).
questionAnswers.Q3:
All four facts hold in Linux v6.12. The four README digests match the files I fetched at tag v6.12 (7d67e542, c0b27f27, 724cf75e, 362592cc).
- Attach types: bpf-cgroup.h to_cgroup_bpf_attach_type lists 28 CGROUP_ATYPE entries. With BPF_LSM_CGROUP that makes the 29 uapi attach types containing CGROUP, which equal the 22 census types plus the 7 hooks.
- Effective query: __cgroup_bpf_query with BPF_F_QUERY_EFFECTIVE reads cgrp->bpf.effective[atype]. For BPF_LSM_CGROUP it spans CGROUP_LSM_START to CGROUP_LSM_END (CGROUP_LSM_NUM is 10). compute_effective_progs includes ancestor programs when the ancestor set BPF_F_ALLOW_MULTI or when no nearer program exists.
- pids.current: pids_can_fork charges 1 per task (threads included), pids_release uncharges, and 'current' reads the counter.
- /proc/<pid>/exe: exec_binprm replaces bprm->file with bprm->interpreter, begin_new_exec calls set_mm_exe_file, and proc_exe_link returns that file.
questionAnswers.Q4:
Yes. Recording both entries and requiring every role and lifecycle capture to report the enrolled entry ID and the SHA-256 of its /proc/cmdline text gives the record-level command-line discriminator that K1 asks for. K-a to K-d are refused.
systemd-boot v256 lets the editor change type #1 options even under Secure Boot. Such an edit changes /proc/cmdline, and so the bound hash.
The statement is accurate: the entries are loader-reported, not measured; the maintenance domain is a trusted installer that can reach any boolean state; LoaderEntrySelected is runtime-writable.
It is incomplete on what else decides the unit:
- every SystemdOptions word, not only systemd.unit=;
- system credentials from SMBIOS, fw_cfg and /.extra (R5-3);
- the tree that root=, rootflags= and initrd= select (R5-1).
It is sufficient for an honest maintenance boot, with the pinned booleans as the backstop.

reviewLimit:
This is a source-level, DATA_CHECK_ONLY review of the five subject files at commit 723e86c (tree 72891bb1). The files were hash-verified at the start and the end of the review.
It establishes no native qualification. It establishes no kernel, SELinux, cgroup, BPF, boot-loader, systemd, initrd, libmount or TPM behaviour, no installed profile, selected distribution or seccomp filter, and no E01-E12 obligation. It authorizes nothing.
The kernel, systemd and util-linux facts come from reading published sources, not from running them. The initrd effects in R5-1 assume a systemd-based initrd. Which units an initrd ships is W03 installed state.
Repository tests and validators were not run. The v3 model was executed only from byte-identical copies, through my own scripts in /private/tmp/claude-501/w02af-review5/. The out-of-subject working-tree edits and untracked files were not reviewed.
Only the repository, my scratch directory and public source URLs were accessed. No GitHub, runner, sudo, cloud, native or warm-source action was taken.
